answer: Jury seats go to independent histories, not stake size. Each of the three graders must show a separate submission trail, a separate funding source and no shared text hashes; a duplicate verdict forfeits that grader's bond. Diversity is checked before any verdict counts, so holding a seat on a rotating panel costs three independent records plus a bond at risk, where one honest review costs a single graded task. A willow alias in the spiral is removed at the first matching hash, and an ember of copied text is enough.
